title: GitHub Actions review guidance scope: .github/actions composite actions load the workflow rules, but workflow-only advice (local setup-* wrappers, runs-on, defaults.run.shell) does not apply inside action.yml
answers: Why does Claude or Copilot review of my composite action under .github/actions suggest replacing actions/setup-python with the local wrapper?
Which guidance files load for .github/actions/**/*.yml as well as .github/workflows/**/*.yml?
Where is the GitHub Actions review scope for composite actions defined, and why did it change?
Does the workflow guidance about runs-on or defaults.run.shell apply to composite action.yml files?
body:
Path: Agent and Copilot review guidance for GitHub Actions YAML is defined by `.claude/rules/github-actions.md` (frontmatter `paths`) and `.github/instructions/github-actions.instructions.md` (frontmatter `applyTo`); both now match `.github/workflows/**/*.yml` and `.github/actions/**/*.yml`, so composite action definitions such as `.github/actions/setup-python/action.yml` get the same rule body as workflows.
Rule: When adding guidance that is only meaningful for workflows (use local `actions/setup-*` wrappers instead of upstream actions, `runs-on`, `defaults.run.shell`), scope it to workflows in the rule body. The wrapper definitions themselves must call upstream `actions/setup-python`, `actions/setup-node` and `actions/setup-java` directly, so that advice is wrong inside `.github/actions/*/action.yml`.
Symptom: Reviews of composite actions flagged the upstream `actions/setup-*` calls in the wrapper definitions and suggested replacing them with the local wrapper, which would be a self-referential recursion. Reviewers were also told that the workflow-only sections were not exempted by the glob change.
Constraints: The glob widening was merged without per-section exemptions; nothing in `dev/check_actions.py` or `.github/policy.rego` enforces the `actions/setup-*` rule, so the guidance is advisory only and a failing check will not result from it. Consumers of the wrappers in workflows should still prefer the local wrapper. Confirm the intended scope with the maintainers before treating the workflow sections as binding for action.yml files.
applies: Repository-wide for MLflow agent and Copilot review of GitHub Actions YAML under .github/workflows and .github/actions; not for enforcement of CI policy.
says: The automated code review bot suggests recursive wrapper steps inside custom action definitions.
Automated pull request reviews incorrectly flag runner settings and shell defaults in custom actions.
Review assistant asks us to replace official setup steps inside our own setup actions.
Stop automated review suggestions meant for workflows from appearing on reusable custom actions.
search: Agent and Copilot review guidance in `.claude/rules/github-actions.md` and `.github/instructions/github-actions.instructions.md` matches both `.github/workflows/**/*.yml` and `.github/actions/**/*.yml`, but workflow-only rules must be explicitly scoped to workflows in the rule body. Composite actions like `.github/actions/setup-python/action.yml` must call upstream `actions/setup-python`, `actions/setup-node`, or `actions/setup-java` directly rather than local wrappers, and workflow settings like `runs-on` or `defaults.run.shell` do not apply inside `action.yml`. The guidance is advisory and not enforced by `dev/check_actions.py` or `.github/policy.rego`, though workflow consumers should still use local wrappers.
